issues.where: C:/Users/UpgradePC/konyvelo_app/kod/backend/src/routes/auth.ts – POST /auth/login/totp (`if (u.lockedUntil && u.lockedUntil > now) throw E.rateLimited`) together with the lock logic in POST /auth/login
issues.what: Anyone who knows a 2FA user's e-mail can keep that user from signing in, without knowing the password. 10 wrong passwords from 3 addresses set users.locked_until for 15 minutes. The password step exempts addresses the owner used before, but the TOTP step refuses everybody while the lock is on. Verified locally on the real build (STAFF_TOTP_REQUIRED=true): accountant from his usual address, right password -> mfa_required, right TOTP code -> 429 with Retry-After 869 s. In production every accountant, admin and team member must use 2FA, so 10 requests per 15 minutes shut the whole staff out of the panel (staff sessions idle out after 12 h). A password reset clears the lock only until the next 10 tries.
issues.fix: In /auth/login/totp do not apply the password-failure lock: reaching this step already proves the password. Keep a separate lock that only wrong TOTP codes set (e.g. users.totp_locked_until), or at least skip locked_until when knownAddress(u.id, ipHmac) is true, as the password step does. Add a test: 10 wrong passwords from 3 addresses, then the owner finishes the TOTP sign-in from a known address.

issues.where: C:/Users/UpgradePC/konyvelo_app/kod/backend/src/auth/codes.ts (per-address budgets: 5 guesses per code, 20 per address per day) and routes/auth.ts POST /auth/password/forgot (forgot-mail-all 12 per hour, in memory) + POST /auth/password/reset
issues.what: The 6-digit password-reset code can be guessed in a distributed way. Since round 1 every requesting address gets its own code with its own 5 guesses; the only per-account cap is 12 codes per hour. Measured locally with a fresh address per code: 288 codes and 1 152-1 440 compared guesses in 24 h against one account, i.e. about 0.12-0.14 % takeover chance per account per day (about 4 % per month for one targeted account; with 1 000 clients roughly one account per day). Clients have no mandatory 2FA, and the new password also opens the GDPR export (ID photos, tax id). The many addresses do not even need a botnet, because the API accepts cross-site text/plain posts (next issue): visitors of any web page can be made to ask for codes and send guesses.
issues.fix: Raise the entropy instead of only counting: mail a long one-time token (128 bit) as a link / deep link, and keep the typed code only as a fallback with an account-wide persistent cap (e.g. 15 wrong comparisons per e-mail per 24 h over all addresses, stored in the DB), or make the typed code 8-9 alphanumeric characters. Lower and persist forgot-mail-all (e.g. 5 per hour). Add a test that 72+ addresses over 24 h cannot exceed the cap.

issues.where: C:/Users/UpgradePC/konyvelo_app/kod/backend/src/http/core.ts readJson (no Content-Type check) and the raw body parser of POST /auth/refresh in routes/auth.ts; affects /auth/login, /auth/register, /auth/password/forgot, /auth/password/reset, /auth/login/totp, /auth/google, /auth/apple
issues.what: JSON endpoints parse any content type, so other websites can post to them from a visitor's browser (form with enctype text/plain, or fetch in no-cors mode; no CORS preflight happens). Verified locally: POST /auth/login with Content-Type text/plain, Origin https://evil.example -> 200 and Set-Cookie __Host-kj_rt. Verified on live with a non-existent address: text/plain is parsed (401, not 415). Consequences: (1) login CSRF - a visitor is silently signed in to the attacker's account on the app or panel host and may then upload ID photos and receipts into an account the attacker controls; (2) any page can make its visitors send forgot / reset / register requests, so the per-IP limits are bypassed with other people's addresses (feeds the reset-code guessing above, mail flooding, accountant capacity).
issues.fix: Answer 415 unless Content-Type is application/json on every JSON route (a form cannot send it, and fetch with it needs a CORS preflight that fails because the API sends no CORS headers). On the cookie-setting /auth/* routes also refuse requests with Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site or with an Origin that is not APP_PUBLIC_URL / PANEL_PUBLIC_URL / API_PUBLIC_URL (native apps send no Origin). Add tests for both.

issues.where: C:/Users/UpgradePC/konyvelo_app/kod/backend/src/routes/me.ts POST /me/consents; C:/Users/UpgradePC/konyvelo_app/kod/backend/src/services/contracts.ts storeSignedContract; services/onboarding.ts stepLockKeys (no lock for 'szerzodes')
issues.what: The megbízási szerződés can be accepted by an account whose e-mail was never confirmed and whose data form is empty. /me/* has no verified-e-mail gate and POST /me/consents checks no step order. issues.fix: For role client in POST /me/consents: require a confirmed e-mail (409 email_not_verified, like /client/*) and require the adatok step to be kesz before megbizasi_szerzodes is accepted (add the lock to stepLockKeys and call assertStepOpen(…, 'szerzodes')). issues.where: C:/Users/UpgradePC/konyvelo_app/kod/backend/src/app.ts (upload-slot middleware keyed on the Bearer token hash) and files/upload.ts withUploadSlot (UPLOAD_SLOTS = 2, wait 45 s); C:/Users/UpgradePC/konyvelo_app/kod/deploy/kezjegy.caddy (upload bodies are streamed, no receive deadline)
issues.what: One client account can block uploads for everybody. A slot is held while the server waits for the request body, there are only 2 slots, and the per-caller rule is keyed on the access token, so one user with two tokens (login + refresh) is two callers. Verified locally on a real HTTP server: two multipart uploads of one account that send a few bytes and then stall -> another client's 1 KB attachment waits 45 s and gets 429. Each stalled request holds its slot up to Node's 300 s request timeout and can be reopened at once. Needs only a confirmed client account (also unpaid, in onboarding); it stops receipts, KYC photos, EV-bejelentés uploads and chat attachments for all users.
issues.fix: Key the per-caller slot on the user id (after auth), not on the token. Do not hold a global slot while bytes are still arriving: let Caddy buffer upload bodies before proxying (request_buffers on the upload matchers) or abort an upload that is not complete within a deadline (e.g. 60-90 s, 408) so a stalled sender frees the slot. Add a test with a stalled multipart request.

issues.where: C:/Users/UpgradePC/konyvelo_app/kod/backend/src/routes/client.ts uploadLimit (600 uploads per hour per user) and POST /client/attachments (open before activation); files/storage.ts; no quota code anywhere in backend/src
issues.what: There is no storage quota and no free-space guard. Any client with a confirmed e-mail (also unpaid, in onboarding) can store 600 x 25 MB = 15 GB per hour as chat attachments that never have to be attached to a message. The disk (179 GB free) is shared with Gardoko and both databases: one account fills it in about 12 hours, a few accounts in about one hour, and a full disk stops Kézjegy and Gardoko. The only disk check is in backup.sh, whose cron is not installed. Not reachable by outsiders on the live DEMO (they cannot confirm an e-mail), but it is the production path.
issues.fix: Add a byte quota per client (e.g. 300 MB before activation, a few GB after; env-configurable), an hourly byte budget per user, and refuse uploads with a clear message when free space on FILES_DIR is under about 10 %. Count unattached uzenet_csatolmany files against the quota and retire those older than 24 h. Show the disk state on the admin Rendszer page independent of backup.sh.

issues.where: C:/Users/UpgradePC/konyvelo_app/kod/app/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml (android:allowBackup="true"); C:/Users/UpgradePC/konyvelo_app/kod/app/app.config.ts has no allowBackup setting
issues.what: The Android app allows system backup of its data. The refresh token is in expo-secure-store (keystore-bound, so a restored copy is unusable and can cause restore errors), and other app data would go into device / cloud backups. issues.where: C:/Users/UpgradePC/konyvelo_app/kod/backend/src/services/tax.ts (recalcYear skips approved quarters; computeYear feeds no approved sums) + C:/Users/UpgradePC/konyvelo_app/kod/ado-motor/src/engine/year.ts (priorBase / priorSzja are always the engine's own recomputed values)
issues.what: Quarter boundary: revenue that lands in an already approved quarter silently vanishes from every payable (or is charged twice in the opposite direction). Reproduced on the local harness with the real backend: (1) Réka, Q3 approved and paid: moving her 1 840 000 Ft item from 2026-10-31 to 2026-09-30 (the designed 'írd át a kivonat szerinti napra' flow) drops the Q4 estimate from 407 874 to 352 674 Ft while Q3 stays 492 054 Ft, so 55 200 Ft SZJA-előleg is never requested. (2) Kata: adding 1 000 000 Ft received 2026-09-20 changes nothing (Q3 stays 510 471, Q4 stays 392 661), so 82 500 Ft SZJA-előleg is missing. No warning for the accountant in either case. The same applies to TB/szocho bases and to manual overrides at approval, which are not carried into the next quarter. NAV 100. füzet 4. and 6.1: the cumulative amount is reduced by what was actually taken into account in earlier quarters, so the shortfall belongs in the next quarter (or the earlier quarter must be reopened / self-revised). The demo's own timeline makes this the normal case: Q3 letter dated 5 Oct, September bank statement requested for 10 Oct.
issues.fix: For every approved (and especially filed) quarter pass the actually approved base sum and SZJA advance to the engine as the prior sums (generalise priorOverrides to per-quarter 'actuals'), so the next open quarter picks up the difference. In addition, when the recomputed result of an approved quarter differs from its approved amounts, raise an accountant warning/flag ('jóváhagyott negyedév adata változott: nyisd újra vagy önellenőrzés'). Add tests for both directions (move into / out of an approved quarter).
